moat_against: Commodity fabrication products — low switching costs; competition from Wieland, Cambridge-Lee, Cerro Flow and imports
Earnings leveraged to COMEX copper and the construction cycle (roughly half of demand construction-linked); FY2017 owner's earnings were negative
Headline revenue growth is inflated by copper price pass-through (COMEX +30.6% YoY in Q2 2026), not volume alone
Gross margin volatile — Q2 2026 27.7% vs 31.0% a year earlier; prior-year quarter included a $36.3M insurance gain
No recurring revenue or contractual lock-in — returns depend on sustaining a favorable metal spread
moat_for: Only vertically integrated North American manufacturer of copper tube & fittings, brass rod and forgings — structural scale/cost position
ROIC proxy 33–49% across FY2021–25 and 12–18% in the soft FY2016–20 years (fundamentals.json) — above the cost of capital through a cycle
Pricing power via copper cost pass-through with spread capture — operating margin expanded from 10.3% (FY2020) to 22.9% TTM
Net-cash balance sheet ($1.367B cash, no debt filed at FY2025) funds dividends, buybacks and accretive M&A (Bison Metals, Chicago Extruded Metals)
Established wholesale distribution and spec position in plumbing/HVACR; US tariffs on semi-finished copper imports favor the domestic footprint
moat_justification: Dominant, vertically integrated North American copper tube/fittings and brass franchise with ROIC well above the cost of capital through the cycle, but the products are commodity fabrications with low switching costs and earnings are leveraged to copper prices and the construction cycle.
name: Mueller Industries, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality cyclical metals franchise, moat 6/10 — on the post-split TTM base it does not clear 15% at $60.07 (weighted IRR 9.9%, weighted IV@15% $33.78); it clears 15% only at or below ~$33.78.
sector: Industrials / Nonferrous metals — copper, brass & piping products
